replies.author: OwnEquipment6863
replies.body:
Interesting.

The subject matter is kind of out of my interests, but there are definitely some huge positives im getting from first 5 minutes.

Love the 'cutscene' with a popup image and text dialogue that reads out letter by letter.

I liked that 'parody tweet' popup. Fun. Looked good.

I like making decisions, but the screen for that type of decision making I think might need to be clearly visually different. Right now the UI stays the same throughout and doesn't feel like it changes 'game modes' per se. If they felt more like important events by having a different ui that isnt shared by everything (ex. the bars at the top), it might hit harder.

Overall very promising.

replies.author: mlbstrike2027
replies.body:
Thank you, this is really helpful feedback. 

We want important events and decisions to feel heavier than normal dialogue, so this is a great nudge in that direction. 

Really appreciate you playing

comments.author: aznkingkong
comments.body: Hey there! Our game [Small Fishes Online](http://seasthebooty.com) is a chill fishing rpg, inspired by Terraria/Stardew/Pokemon. Lots to do, collect things at your own pace. It’s currently in beta but we’ve got active players competing in our leaderboards. Feel free to check it out!

replies.author: OwnEquipment6863
replies.body:
The overall look is great. Love the art, looks damn near hand-painted.

UI and tutorials were a little bit broken for my browser and might need to be shorter, bold the important words you most need to communicate to the player.

The concept and theme is really strong, but I've always loved fishing in games so maybe that's biased.

You could use some more 'fanfare' and particle feedback when you succeed or fail an event or gameplay check. That type of player interaction feedback will make it feel 2x more polished. Players love dopamine buttons like this.

I think the fishing minigame is the thing I would love to see changed a bit. For a game where fishing is kind of the main theme, the minigame feels weaker than it should be. It feels very low stakes and not very interactive. Having a more interactive gameplay experience rather than just timing a button press will go a long way. If you are hesitant to add different gameplay, even just making your current reeling mechanic more in depth (like requiring multiple stages of hitting sweet spots) could help a lot.

Overall, your art looks great, would love to see some more interactive gameplay styles.

replies.author: aznkingkong
replies.body:
Thank you for taking the time to check out and provide such great feedback!! Yes! the art is a mix of hand-drawn and AI-assisted, so I have a decent reptitive style going on in the game.

Noted on the feedback, I definitley feel you there. I think maybe the game itself is more grindy, so a lot of the bigger elements are hidden behind future levels/zones. Like the rarity of fish introduces different elements, as does later stages. There are hidden "Boss" fishes later on that have multiple elements that impact the reel, and have multi-stage catch mechanics too. So I think maybe from my initial design perspective, I was trying to hide those "surprise" elements more. 

I do agree with you though - the more I can capture attention in the beginning, the better it can be. Once again, thank you for your help!

comments.author: South3rs
comments.body: Hey that’s cool. Mine is an early work in progress and might not be your thing (it’s a WW2 RTS) but please feel free to try it at fieldofcommand.com. I’d love feedback from people especially on the art side as I’m struggling with that

replies.author: OwnEquipment6863
replies.body:
Wow I have to say I was NOT expecting something this good to pop up out of nowhere. This is very VERY impressive. 🙌🥳

Art looks great, both the title screen and the 3d RTS game. The RTS game is very responsive and very fun. I feel like im play a proper Warhammer/C&C/Starcraft game. Really amazing work.

I love that its voice acted to, the voices aren't too weird and the accents fit the theme.

My only issue was that the title screen and opening UI took too long to get through to get to actually playing the game!

I think this has an incredible amount of potential. I was really into starcraft as a kid and wouldve been stoked to play this haha.

I think just streamlining the UI, cutting out what you don't ABSOLUTELY need will help you the most. Design by subtraction.

replies.author: South3rs
replies.body: Thank you so much that’s awesome to hear 🙌 deffo taking that feedback on straight away. I know exactly what you mean about the time it takes to get into the first game. I’m thinking first time players should just get thrown straight into the tutorial battle or something? Or maybe even a little prologue action scene?

comments.author: Fun_Worry_3079
comments.body: I don’t know if you’re into retro-inspired games, but I have a full library of them over at https://orangeheartcreative.itch.io My personal favorites are “KickBrawl: World Tour” and “Birdie Blues and the Jazz Cats.”

replies.author: OwnEquipment6863
replies.body:
Hmm I tried all of them and I can't say I found one that really stuck with me.

Kickbrawl was probably my most played, but I think it could also use some more work. I think maybe you should take one of these games and iterate on it more and more rather than moving onto the next thing. I wasn't really a fan of the art of any of them, but Birdie Blues and the Jazz Cats stuck out to me and did have a cool style in its opening.   
  
How long would you say it takes you to make these? I'm curious how long you're spending on them before you move to the next one.

replies.author: Fun_Worry_3079
replies.body: I spend about three weeks, off and on, working on these games. Then, I'll take about a week off to brainstorm ideas for the next project. I don't intend these games to be full, polished commercial products; this is more of a hobby project for me. Also, these games reflect my philosophy that indie games don't have to be a commercially viable product, but just something fun people can use to pass the time, which is what I hope comes across to people. I'm not selling these games, both literally and figuratively. I'm selling the idea that even someone like me can make games like these, given the right tools and time.

replies.author: OwnEquipment6863
replies.body:
I think for that purpose these games fulfil that wonderfully. Keep up the good work! Ill follow your progress here.   
  
I am curious, do you think you would ever dive more deeply into a single game?

replies.author: Fun_Worry_3079
replies.body: Perhaps, one day, I'll do a deep dive and make a commercial product. As of right now, though, I'm just happy to be part of this community we call game development (even if I am using agentic coding to do it).
